3. The case of the plaintiff-petitioner is that the said suit property measuring 720 ajutangsha originally belonged to one. Shanti Gopal Saha who subsequently transferred the same to Dr Moula Boksha by a sale deed No. 446 dated 23-1-53. Dr Moula Boksha thereafter transferred the said land to Ms Meherunnessa by the sale deed No. 6557 dated 15-12-55 whereupon Meherunnessa had her name recorded in the SA Khatian as owner of 10 annas 13 gandas, 1 kara and 1 kranti out of the total land in the plot measuring 0.80 acres. While Meherunnessa was continuing as owner in possession by paying government rents and dues she transferred the said land to Ms Saleha Khatun (proforma defendant No. 5) by a sale deed No. 207 dated 2-1-62. Saleha Kahtun thereafter mutated her name in the government records and while continuing as the owner in possession by installing electric, gas and WASA connections in her name gifted the same away to the plaintiff-petitioner out of her love and affection. 

 4. The defendant-opposite party No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegations in the plaint contending, inter alias that the entire land in the suit plot measuring 1080 ajutangsha was the khas land of the government. Accordingly, the government settled the same with different persons from time to time and one Nanda Kishore Shah being one of the settlement holders sold his share in the land in the suit plot to one Fazle Rashid by a registered deed No. 7604 dated 16-12-52 and subsequently, the father of the said defendant-opposite party No.1 purchased the same from Fazle Rashid by a registered sale deed No. 5334 dated 14-9-53 and got the same duly recorded in his name and paid rents. The defendant opposite party No.1 inherited the said land after the death of his father and had his name recorded in SA Khatian in respect of the said land and since then he has been owning and possessing specifically one third share of the land in the suit plot. The defendant-opposite party No.1 having subsequently learnt that the suit plot was government khas land prayed for regular settlement of the same and defendant Nos. 2-4 accordingly, settled one third share of the land of the suit plot with the defendant opposite party No.1 on 2-12-81 and since then he has been owning and possessing the same. 

 8. Careful perusal and scrutiny of the record reveals that no basic documents of title were brought on record during the trial in support of the case of the plaintiff-petitioner as regards her title to the suit land. Certified copy of SA Khatian as well as an attested copy of porcha were filed and brought on record by way of exhibits showing that the plaintiff- petitioner acquired 720 Ajutangsha land in the suit plot by virtue of an Osiwatnama followed by an oral gift from the'proforma defendant No. 5, Saleha Kahtoon. In the premises, the trial Court dismissed the suit on the finding that the plaintiff-petitioner failed to prove her title to the suit land in the absence of proof of her basic documents of title to the suit land.
